# airgap-ai-stack

Pack, verify, deploy, and attest open-weight AI models inside enclaves with no internet egress.

## What it does

One Go binary with six commands:
- pack: hash every file in a bundle directory, write manifest.json (GGUF magic checked)
- verify: check presence, size, SHA256 of every manifest entry; flag unlisted files
- check: probe DNS and TCP egress and report no-egress / partial / detected (the attestation probe)
- serve: verify the bundle, then launch any OpenAI-compatible runtime (llama-server, ollama) bound to 127.0.0.1
- eval: run a deterministic eval suite against the local endpoint (contains, contains_any, not_contains, regex, exact; temperature 0; no judge model)
- report: assemble the accreditation markdown (bundle contents, checksums, egress attestation, eval results, host identity)

## Key files

- cmd/airgap/main.go: CLI entry, all six subcommands
- internal/bundle/bundle.go: pack and verify with SHA256 manifest
- internal/egress/egress.go: egress probes with injectable dialer (testable offline)
- internal/eval/eval.go: deterministic eval runner against OpenAI-compatible endpoints
- internal/report/report.go: markdown accreditation report
- examples/bundle/: working sample bundle with the failover-diagnosis eval suite

## Design rules

- Zero third-party dependencies (Go standard library only); eval suites are JSON, not YAML
- Single binary; MIT licence
- The binary makes no network calls except explicit probes (check) and the endpoint you point eval at; serve binds 127.0.0.1
- serve refuses to launch a bundle that fails verification
- Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 usage error

## Test with

go test ./... -count=1
